task_origin_contract.rule: A free-discovery output cannot lose its candidate lifecycle by being repackaged as an ordinary taskbook. If the task exists because of a free candidate, its audited candidate provenance is mandatory.

obvious_stage_continuation_rule.pattern: STAGE integer >= 2 in task_id or title
obvious_stage_continuation_rule.reason: Stage numbering is explicit continuation semantics and may not be relabeled NEW_DIRECTION to bypass the successor gate.

task_lineage_contract.semantic_anti_evasion_rule: Even without Stage naming, if the parent result is a necessary research premise/motivation and the new task is the next unresolved layer of the same mother route, classify it CONTINUATION. Renaming does not reset lineage.
task_lineage_contract.rule: PASS or DONE on a parent task is not itself evidence for a successor. A CONTINUATION taskbook is dispatchable only when its successor gate names a genuine new information gap, falsifiable outcomes, a stop rule, and whether an independent/alternative exploration path was considered.

optional_metadata.identity_lane: compact human-readable lane such as R012, R005C, P017
optional_metadata.parent_task_id: required when task_lineage=CONTINUATION; otherwise normally null
optional_metadata.successor_gate: required when task_lineage=CONTINUATION; otherwise normally null

manual_dispatch_identity_gate: Driver-mediated manual relay must preallocate a Researcher-ID outside the taskbook before user handoff and the receiving final-response footer follows final_response_identity_policy.json.
rules: A taskbook defines task-specific work, not a particular conversation instance and not a copy of repository operating policy.

Every newly authored or re-reviewed dispatchable taskbook carries final_response_identity_policy=INHERIT_GLOBAL so a strict taskbook-only execution packet still exposes the existence of the mandatory final-output identity contract without copying its template text into the mathematical body.
Every newly authored taskbook declares task origin and task lineage. A free-candidate origin preserves audited candidate provenance; a continuation preserves parent/successor provenance.
CONTINUATION requires parent_task_id and a complete successor_gate; stage numbering or parent PASS is never a substitute for the gate.
An obvious Stage 2+ task is CONTINUATION by construction and cannot be labeled NEW_DIRECTION merely to bypass the gate.
The taskbook body inherits current repository policy through research_taskbook_policy.json; generic rules already visible to the executing researcher must not be restated in the body.
Taskbook authoring uses tools/research_taskbook.py new, followed by task-local editing, machine audit, Driver review, and an approved policy_review stamp before dispatch.
The policy_review digest is derived from the current policy set. If any policy input changes, a previously stamped taskbook becomes stale and must be re-reviewed before another dispatch.

Task-specific instructions that conflict with inherited policy are forbidden unless recorded as a narrow temporary_overrides entry with conflict_id, scope, reason, replacement_behavior, and expires_when.

Temporary overrides alter only the named policy behavior for the declared scope and lifetime; they do not silently weaken theorem truth, safety, authorization, ownership, canonical-promotion requirements, candidate maturity, origin provenance, successor-stage requirements, or final-response identity visibility.

Legacy taskbooks may remain unstamped or lack origin/lineage/footer inheritance as historical artifacts, but any new dispatch of an unstamped/stale legacy taskbook requires current review; newly authored taskbooks must satisfy V6.

Taskbooks never bind a fixed runtime Researcher-ID. For Driver-mediated manual relay, the Driver preallocates one Researcher-ID in a separate dispatch envelope and records it in the relay/handoff. Scheduler CLAIM and direct self-start paths use their own identity bootstrap.

A continuation in the same researcher conversation preserves its existing Researcher-ID; a genuinely new manual dispatch receives a new preallocated Researcher-ID unless explicitly routed to the same conversation.
Researcher identity never grants Driver authority or theorem ownership. Driver conversations use Driver-ID, not Researcher-ID, as their visible identity label.

A free-research axiom candidate enters taskbook authoring only after Phase-B audit and Driver intake under research_axiom_candidate_state_machine.json, and its candidate provenance must remain visible in taskbook metadata.
recommended_flow: for FREE_AXIOM_CANDIDATE origin, supply audited candidate id/state
for CONTINUATION, set --parent-task-id and complete successor_gate including alternative exploration consideration
declare any intentional temporary override in policy_review.temporary_overrides
for Driver-mediated manual relay, preallocate Researcher-ID with tools/research_identity.py and put it in the dispatch envelope
dispatch only after taskbook PASS and identity binding
